headline: Grab chief executive Anthony Tan warned that fast AI adoption could widen the gap between people who benefit and people left behind, pointing to recent unrest in Indonesia.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a regional tech leader's warning on inequality, a view rather than new data.
importance_line: Workers and small businesses without access to AI could fall further behind, but Tan offers a concern, not evidence of unrest caused by AI.
summary: Marketing-Interactive reports that Tan, head of the Southeast Asian ride-hailing and delivery company Grab, told Dow Jones' Risk Journal event in Singapore on 6 Oct 2026 that AI could create a "K-shaped recovery", in which people with access to the technology pull ahead. He pointed to recent unrest in Indonesia as a reminder of how fast economic discontent can escalate and said Grab is building AI tools for small merchants.
notes: WSJ page blocked (401). Same event read at Marketing-Interactive; the WSJ headline's 'social upheaval' wording is not in that text, which speaks of widening divides and unrest in Indonesia.
